draft.title: Koch's postulates
card: Robert Koch, a German doctor, set out steps to show that one particular microbe causes one particular disease.
Step 1 and 2: the microbe is found in every case of the disease and not in healthy hosts. It is then taken from a sick host and grown in pure culture, away from other microbes.
Step 3: the cultured microbe is put into a healthy host. That host must develop the same disease.
Step 4: the microbe is taken from this newly sick host and shown to be the same one that was first grown. Together the steps link the microbe to the disease as its cause.
draft.remember: A microbe is shown to cause a disease when it is found in the sick, grown pure, and then makes a healthy host sick.

a.q: Why does Koch's method grow the microbe in pure culture before testing it in a healthy host?
opts: So the disease can be linked to that microbe alone
So the microbe becomes weaker before it is injected
So the host can build up immunity to the microbe
So the microbe can be seen without a microscope
a.why: A pure culture holds only one type of microbe. If the healthy host then gets sick, the cause must be that microbe and not another one mixed in. Weakening the microbe is not a step, and it would work against showing that it causes disease.
a.clue: What would go wrong if other microbes were mixed in?

b.q: Researchers find bacterium X in every sick sheep on a farm and in no healthy sheep. They grow it in pure culture and inject it into a healthy sheep, which stays well. What does this result show?
opts: X is not shown to cause the disease
X is shown to cause the disease in sheep
X is harmless, because the healthy sheep stayed well
X is shown to cause the disease by growing in culture
b.why: Koch's steps need the cultured microbe to make a healthy host develop the same disease. Here that step failed, so the link is not shown. Finding X in every sick sheep is not enough alone, as it could be a result of the illness or something else could be involved.
b.clue: Which step needs the healthy host to become sick?

a.best: So the disease can be linked to that microbe alone

b.best: X is not shown to cause the disease

problems.detail: The remember line says a microbe is shown to cause a disease once it is found in the sick, grown pure and makes a healthy host sick. That leaves out step 4, re-isolating the same microbe from the newly sick host, which the card says is part of the full set of steps. It also leaves out 'not in healthy hosts'. Students could take this to mean three steps are enough.
